page: Microsoft Azure EC4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache sizing comprises 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. The configuration does not include a GPU.

Resource allocation features a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, providing 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core). For high-speed temporary storage, the instance includes 161 GB of local SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread capability contrasted with limited multi-core throughput due to its low physical core count. The instance achieves an average single-core rating in stress-ng (1986.87) and Geekbench (1189.0), with Geekbench text processing also placing in the middle 50% (1519.0). Conversely, multi-threaded workloads fall into the bottom 25%, as reflected by Geekbench multi-core (2645.0), stress-ng multi-core (3943.74), PassMark CPU (4713.07), and software compilation under Clang (3257.0). Redis SET operations achieved 3.34 million operations per second, which also ranks in the lower quartile.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in local SSD storage, the EC4ads_v5 offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy services that do not require heavy parallel computational throughput. It is functionally suited for medium-scale in-memory caches, relational database instances, memory-intensive analytical processing, and enterprise application hosting requiring local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure EC4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine providing 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Sourced from 2 dedicated physical cores across 4 threads, the instance features 32 MB of L3 cache and includes 161 GB of integrated local SSD storage, with no attached GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate mid-tier single-core performance (Geekbench single-core of 1189.0 and stress-ng score of 1986.87), while multi-threaded benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (3943.74) and Clang compilation (3257.0) align in the lower quartile due to the 2-core physical limit. With an 8.0 GB per-core memory allocation and bundled solid-state scratch space, EC4ads_v5 fits memory-intensive applications, small-to-medium caching nodes, and relational database hosting.
